**Dog was pulled and returned at same time as kennel mate, A5171346 but evaluated individually**
Handlers approached kennel front, dogs were laying on bed together. Lead handler knelt down and began offering treats, dogs were hesitant initially but dog up and began coming forward. Dog stayed away from handler initially, handler sat on chair towards back of room. Handler began offering treats, dog would approach for treats but would not take treats from handlers hands. About 5 minutes into evaluation dog approached handlers shoe and sniffed for a few seconds and then ate a few more treats from the ground. Dog then sat at opposite side of room and began ignoring handler. Handler continued to offer treats, dog ignored them. Handler tried to verbally coax dog would not look at handler. Handler allowed dog a few minutes and then retrieved leash. Handler again held leash taut and scooped up dog. Dog was rigid in posture and thrashed briefly then allowed carrying. Handler saw assistant handler and dogs were returned at the same time. Handler was able to remove leash by hand and place dog in kennel, dog retreated to back and then kennel mate was also returned. Dogs were neutral in posture when reunited.

sections.memo:
9/24/2026
09/24/26 14:08 This dog has demonstrated a persistent, recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 9/29/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 9/30/26 or sooner if warranted.
Intake
3/19/2026
How long have you had the animal?
4 DAYS. DOG WAS ROAMING THE NEIGHBORHOOD, FINDER HAD PUT FOOD OUT AND WAS ABLE TO GET THE DOG TO GO INTO THEIR YARD.
Has the animal been around other animals? What kind of animals? How would you describe the interaction with other animals?
GOOD WITH FEMALE DOG IN HOME. PLAYFUL, TRIED TO MOUNT MULTIPLE TIMES. LOW GROWLS AT OTHER MALE DOG IN THE HOME.
Was the animal around any other people or children? If yes, how would you describe the animals behavior towards other people/children?
NO CONTACT WITH CHILDREN.
Has the animal shown any aggression around other people? Might want to include a few examples of what aggression looks like. Barking, growling, lunging, etc.? If yes, what were the circumstances?
GROWLS ON APPROACH, BUT WARMED UP QUICK.
Did you keep the animal inside or outside?
OUTSIDE
If inside, did you keep the animal in a crate or allowed to roam? Was the animal destructive in any way?
CRATE,CHEWED UP CRATE AND BEDDING. NO OTHER DESTRUCTION.
If outside, what kind of fencing do you have and did it contain the animal?
WOOD FENCE, YARD CONTAINED  DOG.
Did the animal show any aggression, like **growling, curling their lips, lunging** around food, toys, or bones?
GROWLED WHEN DOGS OR PEOPLE CAME NEAR ITS FOOD.
Has the animal shown any signs of illness?
NO SIGNS OF ILLNESS.
Does the animal walk on a leash?
PULLS HARD ON LEASH.
